label: <DEL> step of long sequences (L>=8) whose first token is in a specific set (a,c,d,f,n,q,s,u,v,w,y,0,1)
explanation: Fires only at the delimiter step (100% of mass), i.e. when the model is about to emit original token 0. It needs a long sequence: L=9 holds 72% of mass, L=8 27%, L=7 <1% (weak), and it never fires for L<=6. Within those steps, which token is first (the token about to be recalled) picks out a set: a, c, d, f, n, q, s, u, v, w, y, 0 have about 85-99% firing rate, 1 about 70%, e/i/l/x about 30-45%, and the others almost never fire. Magnitude is higher for L=9 than L=8, and highest when the first token is q, c, n or d. It never fires in the original-input or copy phases. Dev: P=0.91, R=0.81, F1=0.86, mass recall 0.93. Most misses are weak activations on e/i/l/x-first or L=7 sequences.

issues: Confirmed: 100% of the mass is at the delimiter step (phase 1). The feature never fires in the original or copy phases and never fires for L<=6. L=9 holds 72% of mass, L=8 holds 27%, L=7 holds 0.7% (and fires on only 3.1% of L=7 delimiter steps).

The per-first-token firing rates in the explanation average L=8 and L=9 together, which hides a systematic length-by-token interaction. Dev rates for L=9 / L=8: e 0.75/0.13, i 0.77/0.07, l 0.56/0.02, x 0.73/0.07, '1' 0.96/0.43, '2' 0.35/0.00. So e, i, l and x are not 'about 30-45%' everywhere: they fire about 56-77% of the time at L=9 and almost never at L=8. '1' is not 'about 70%': it is 96% at L=9 and 43% at L=8.

Within the core set, L=8 rates are clearly below 85-99% for s (0.69), v (0.70), y (0.73), f (0.77) and '0' (0.88), while at L=9 every core token is about 99-100%. So the claimed rate of about 85-99% for the core set only holds at L=9.

Systematic miss class: L=9 delimiter steps whose first token is e, i, l or x. These are about 70% active and the predicate excludes them. Including them, plus '1' only at L=9, raises test F1 from 0.859 to 0.897 and mass recall from 0.932 to 0.974.

The misses that remain after the fix are mostly weak (about 0.0-0.2 of max) activations on L=7 steps or on borderline tokens. The false positives are scattered over L=8 sequences with borderline tokens. This looks like graded noise.
